criteria.text: Repeated bounded sweep evaluates monitoring events.
Trip → repair attempt 1 succeeds → original proposal/config stays, event terminal, original proposal settled active, no revert/alert.
Trip → 3 repairs fail → auto-revert → original config restored → original proposal reverted → alert persisted.
No breach + expired window → clear → original proposal active → no repair/revert; later outcomes cannot reopen.
No recursive monitoring of auto-repair proposals.
Legacy measureProposal must not race/settle an enrolled proposal while event is monitoring/tripped.
SQLite/local-only. Postgres skips enrollment/sweep; never rely on in-memory fallback in production wiring.
Trigger failures are non-fatal per-event and logs contain IDs/safe outcomes only.
New event/alert/repair audit/log records contain no raw diagnosis context, prompts, secret-shaped patch values, snapshots, or unrestricted error strings.
A successful eligible approval creates a post-apply event and scheduler owns evaluation through the actual sandboxed API/bootstrap.
criteria.reason: Passed against the isolated sandbox on ports 4098/4097.

criteria.text: A lifecycle enrollment rejection after the approval mutation/claim committed is isolated for both generic and scope exits: return the committed successful HTTP response, log only proposal ID plus a fixed safe outcome, and do not start legacy measurement under ambiguous enrollment ownership.
criteria.reason: Table-driven route test injects a secret-bearing rejection after durable refine-config and scope commits, mocks the org_proposal_measure.measureProposal module seam before importing the controller, and for both controller branches asserts HTTP 200, persisted mutation/status, exact redacted warning, and zero legacy measurement calls. Explicitly invoking that bound mock made both rows fail before the falsification was restored.

criteria.text: The scheduler defers tripped events while diagnosis is unready, isolates per-event trigger rejection, rejects overlapping sweeps, and honors the requested bounded repository limit.
criteria.reason: Each property has a dedicated integration test using the real SQLite repository and lifecycle composition.

criteria.text: Legacy measureProposal skips lifecycle-owned proposals in both monitoring and tripped states without invoking measurement/revert dependencies or changing proposal/config state.

Second pass: the scheduler sweep re-invokes the repair state machine on EVERY tick for a tripped, non-terminal event (not only when no repair has ever been attempted), so real evidence-gated advance/repair/exhaust actually progresses across real sweep ticks.
criteria.reason: Passed against an isolated sandbox on ports 4297/4298/4299 (distinct from any concurrently running worktree sandbox). See docs/ai/contracts/issue-1433.json's issue-1433-c11.

criteria.text: THIRD PASS (finding #5): the live E2E's final resolution assertion requires the EXACT persisted terminal state after real clean evidence is fed — guardrail_status='clear', revert_status='not_needed', repair_attempt_count equal to the exact repair-proposal-id trail length, that trail unchanged from the landed-attempt checkpoint, no alert payload, and the original proposal settled 'active' (never 'reverted') — not merely 'the recheck floor changed,' which an ADVANCING (still-breaching, next-attempt) outcome could also produce and would incorrectly read as a pass under the prior assertion.
criteria.reason: Passed in the isolated 4297/4298/4299 sandbox with a synthetic DB and disposable OpenAI MRU model: actual post-apply-regression guardrail signals produced a real diagnosis and repair proposal; the event stayed tripped across a cron tick with no post-repair evidence; five clean outcomes then settled guardrail_status=clear, revert_status=not_needed, an unchanged one-repair trail, no alert, and the original proposal active. 1/1 live test passed in 160.53s.
